texts: good. the cold snap's arrival, its 'first' rank, the Year 2 restriction on that rank, and the past tense are all recorded, and the light verb 'came' correctly puts the time straight on the snap rather than inventing a separate coming event. One caveat you cannot write around: 'day 395 of Year 2' has to go into the calendar day-of-month slot, because the notation has no day-of-year term.

good. it parses as a fireable rule over lanterns on the Cliff Path, carrying the salt-bloom, the lantern's own mire-essence as where it sat, the 'already' presupposition and the 'every' quantifier word.
good. it parses as a strength-zero rule over exactly the lanterns the previous sentence established, with the 'no' quantifier recorded, and 'went out' is kept whole rather than swapped for a synonym.

bad: 'the lanterns OF the three bright stations' is recorded as the lanterns being located INSIDE the stations, a spatial containment you never state; the per-lantern rule also mints each lantern's extra essence without ever saying it is mire-essence. Rewrite with the possessive, which cannot be misread as a place: 'The three bright stations' lanterns burned extra mire-essence.'

good. the producing, the strong mist-light and the per-lantern rule are all covered, and the lanterns resolve to the same set as the previous sentence. If you rewrite that sentence's of-phrase, use the identical wording here so both mentions still land on one set of lanterns.

good. the showing, the mist-light and the 'at night' slot are recorded, with a per-lantern rule beside the group event. The rule leaves the light it mints for each lantern untyped, but that is a translator slip rather than anything your wording causes.

bad: 'crowds' is plural, but it collapses to a single crowd - the instruction set has no form for a group whose members are themselves groups - so the passage loses the fact that there was more than one crowd, and the later 'the nightmoth crowds' binds to that one symbol too. If the crowds are one per station, write 'At each bright station, the strong mist-light attracted a crowd of nightmoths.' - that is an ordinary per-station rule and gives you one crowd per station.

mixed: the per-station counting comes through as a fireable rule with the keepers, the nightmoths and 'each' all carried, but 'about thirty' has to be stored as a spread inside a count slot specified to take a plain integer, and 'per night' can only be recorded as 'the counting recurred nightly' rather than as a nightly rate. If an exact figure is acceptable in your world, 'Keepers counted thirty nightmoths at each bright station every night.' parses cleanly.

mixed: the crowd, the Middle Row, and the six-of-ten night sets are recorded, but nothing says the ten nights are the ones FOLLOWING day 395 ('next' has no carrier), and the six nights end up hanging off one gathering event in a time slot meant for calendar terms rather than giving six occasions. Rewrite with explicit days: 'Between day 396 and day 405 of Year 2, a crowd of nightmoths gathered at the Middle Row on six nights.' - day bounds are encodable where 'the next ten nights' is not.

mixed: the descent, the sky-cat group, the cliff-spires as source and the per-cat rule are all covered, and 'those six nights' correctly resolves to the set from the previous sentence, but one descent event stands in for six nights' worth. Rewrite as 'On each of those six nights, sky-cats descended from the cliff-spires.' - the explicit 'each of' gives one descent per night instead of one for all six.

bad: 'the nightmoth crowds' collapses onto the single crowd introduced earlier, so the plurality is lost, and the six nights again hang off one hunting event. Rewrite as 'On each of those six nights, the sky-cats hunted the nightmoth crowd at the Middle Row.' - one hunt per night against that night's crowd; the Middle Row location is already carried correctly and should stay where it is.

mixed: the molting is recorded as happening during the hunting, with a per-cat rule, but 'the hunts' (plural) binds to the single hunt event, so the separate hunts are never distinguished. Rewrite as 'On each of those six nights, the sky-cats molted during the hunt.' - that lines one molting up with one hunt per night.

good. the feathers are a group with a per-feather rule, the base is correctly recorded as part of the cliff, the base is the destination of the fall, and the feathers are the thing that undergoes the fall rather than an actor.

good. the harvest, its feather_harvest to harvest genus, the past-tense 'strong' verdict, and the one-month gap after the feathers fell are all recorded - the measured gap is used because no month is ever named in the passage, which is the right fallback.
